title: Reconcile compliance log gaps after ingest surge overlapping with key-rotation window
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-traffic tenant onboarding surge on 2026-02-12, the audit-log ingestion pipeline experienced sustained backpressure. Concurrently, an automated KMS key-rotation job ran across several ingestion instances. The combination produced a ~27-minute window where some audit events were acknowledged by the edge proxies but failed to be durably persisted to the compliance store. Impact: partial loss of audit chronology for a small subset of customers (estimated <0.2% of events in the affected window). This ticket tracks reconciliation, validation, and preventive engineering and ops actions to close the gap and reduce recurrence risk.
action_items: [Marco Chen] Create a reconciliation run that replays edge journal segments against the canonical store; prioritize windows 2026-02-12 03:10:00 - 03:40:00 UTC; due 2026-02-20 (in progress)
[Sana Iqbal] Extend ingest pipeline metrics to surface 'acknowledged-but-not-durable' counts and emit an alert when >1000 events/min for 5m; due 2026-03-01
[DevOps] Harden key-rolling orchestration to quiesce ingestion workers before epoch handoff; add graceful drain step with timeout and safe-rollback; due 2026-03-10
[Observability] Add a cross-service chronological-sanity check job that runs daily and produces mismatch diffs; store diffs in a dedicated S3 bucket and dashboard; due 2026-03-05
[PM] Draft customer communication and compliance memo for auditors describing incident, reconciliation methodology, and mitigations; due 2026-03-08
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial investigation shows ingestion backlog coincided with a scheduled KMS rolling rotation. Edge proxies acked events but the ingestion workers were briefly unable to complete writes due to a lock in the log-writer component.

2026-02-17 - Marco Chen: Reconciliation prototype completed. It can locate missing sequence ranges from edge journals and replay them to the store idempotently. Found 1,843 candidate events; sampling indicates 96% are recoverable without conflict.

2026-02-18 - Sana Iqbal: Metrics spike dashboard: ingested-but-not-durable metric added to staging and alert threshold tuned. We intentionally hide noise from normal bursts by requiring sustained >5m signal.

2026-02-20 - Marco Chen: Reconciliation run 1 finished: 1,782 events re-applied, 61 events excluded due to sequence overlap with later writes. Generated reconciliation report and upload to drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/recon/ENG-96123/run-1-report
2026-02-22 - Compliance (J. Morales): Reviewed reconciliation sampling and requested cryptographic proof-of-write for a subset of re-applied events; added as follow-up requirement.
2026-02-25 - DevOps (L. Nguyen): Implemented quiesce step in key-rotation job and added a conservative 90s drain window. Staged rollout to canary cluster succeeded.
2026-02-28 - Marco Chen: Nightly sanity-check job prototype pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/log-tools/pull/412. Needs perf tuning before enabling globally.
2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Preparing compliance memo draft and review with legal next week. Marking security review required for any changes that change persistence guarantees.
